headline: UK start-up Parallel Carbon pairs direct air capture with green-hydrogen electrolysis to chase sub-US$100/t CO2
summary: Manchester-based Parallel Carbon uses a membraneless electrolyser that splits a neutral-salt electrolyte into acid and alkali (no chlorine) to co-produce green hydrogen while a mineral sorbent captures CO2 from air and is regenerated by the acid; it targets <US$100/t capture and ~US$1/kg hydrogen, runs a small Manchester pilot, and has pre-sold 1,200 t of durable removal to Zurich Insurance.
co2crc_note: Novel low-cost DAC + green-hydrogen co-production route to track against CO2CRC's capture-materials and DAC research remit.
extractor_note: C&EN start-ups-to-watch profile; cost/performance figures are company targets, not independently verified. Hydrogen co-production falls outside the CCS value_chain vocabulary.

headline: The Government cannot pull the plug on Humber carbon capture and hydrogen - Humber Energy Board chair
summary: Richard Gwilliam, chair of the Humber Energy Board, argues the UK government risks regional deindustrialisation if the Humber is left out of CCS/hydrogen cluster support after the ~GBP22bn committed this year went to Teesside and Merseyside; business groups say they are ready to invest >GBP15bn if a CO2 transport-and-storage network, hydrogen markets and grid upgrades are backed, with a decision expected before year-end.
co2crc_note: UK cluster-funding sequencing and regional social-licence pressure - a live template for how Australia phases CCS-hub support and manages regions left outside the first funding wave.
extractor_note: Opinion is pro-CCS advocacy; negative tone reflects the warning over government funding neglect, not opposition to CCS. The GBP22bn (cluster-funding aggregate) and >GBP15bn (potential private investment) are context, not a discrete new commitment, so amount is null.

headline: CNOOC passes a milestone on China's first offshore CO2-injection platform for enhanced gas recovery (Dongfang 1-1)
summary: Upstream reported a milestone on CNOOC's Dongfang 1-1 CO2-injection project off Hainan in the South China Sea - China's first offshore carbon-injection-for-enhanced-gas-recovery demonstration; Chinese state media dated completion of the ~17,000-tonne platform's main structure and entry into commissioning to ~4 October. Designed to store >1 Mtpa of CO2 beneath the seabed once operational.
co2crc_note: China's first offshore CO2-EGR demonstration - a direct comparator for Australia's offshore depleted-reservoir storage ambitions (CarbonNet, Bonaparte, Bayu-Undan).
extractor_note: Radar near-miss: Upstream coverage dated 12 Oct, but the underlying platform main-structure-completion/commissioning milestone is ~4 Oct (out of the 12-13 Oct window). capacity_mtpa 1.0 is a stated design target, not an operating figure.

headline: Carbon Clean joins Net Zero Innovation Hub to bring carbon capture to data centres
summary: Capture-technology firm Carbon Clean said it has joined a Net Zero Innovation Hub initiative to adapt modular carbon capture for data-centre power and backup generation, an emerging demand segment as AI load growth strains grids.
co2crc_note: Emerging data-centre / AI-load capture application niche for compact modular capture systems.
extractor_note: Radar near-miss: dated 6 Oct, just outside the 12-13 Oct window.
